clearedSpotChecks.check: L-965 Tasks 2 to 4 on Robinhood Chain: 185 flagged rows, 184 collectProtocolFees and 1 token-moved, where token 0x7743d98038d6b4f05072b9eaafb76dbe9eff30ee burned 463.587 units from the PoolManager through burn(address,uint256) called by 0x589f03fa49dae74d970113734984ef63a75f5c04 (transaction 0x5c4df554..., block 4,607,805), an issuer power.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I queried https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com. eth_getTransactionByHash gives block 0x464f3d (4,607,805), from 0x589f03fa49dae74d970113734984ef63a75f5c04, to the token, input selector 0x9dc29fac with the PoolManager 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951 as the account and 0x19219020e0febf7ba8 (463.587e18) as the amount. The receipt holds one log, a Transfer from the PoolManager to address 0, and no PoolManager log. eth_call owner() at latest returns 0x589f03fa49dae74d970113734984ef63a75f5c04. The same burn by 0x1111...1111 reverts with OwnableUnauthorizedAccount (0x118cdaa7), and by the owner reverts with ERC20InsufficientBalance (0xe450d38c), because the PoolManager now holds none. The burn is therefore owner gated, and the actor is issuer. Historical state at that block is not served and debug_traceTransaction does not exist on this endpoint, so I could not read the balance before and after; the receipt is enough for the class. The token symbol is POPCATHOOD, a token the victims chose to hold, so this is a single token hazard.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-965 Tasks 2 to 4 on Ethereum: 9,402 flagged rows classified into recorded token classes and protocol fee collection; the open row 0x23919165b52da8ef9a2b080c4470454485d091aa1f3b037ad3d8cc7303a6d67d at block 25,852,472 is the F-079 vesting token 0x177d39ac676ed1c67a2b268ad7f1e58826e5b0af and the PoolManager balance of that token is the same before and after (124,163.65e18).
clearedSpotChecks.note: On https://mainnet.gateway.tenderly.co, balanceOf(PoolManager) of 0x177d39ac676ed1c67a2b268ad7f1e58826e5b0af is 0x1a4aecd652ac4ec5441d (124,163.65e18) at block 25,852,471 and at block 25,852,472, so nothing of that token left the PoolManager in the block. The receipt (status 1, from 0x7f881d3e..., to 0x00000f91109c4d0007e90000d9facad5298a0cac) shows a loop of token Transfer logs in which each step logs one transfer into the PoolManager, a token specific event 0xf9565aec, and two Transfer logs out of the PoolManager for the same amount, doubling each round. Each outward move is logged twice, so the census counts outflow that did not happen. Two PoolManager Swap logs of pool 0xf9346b8d... bracket the loop: the first pays the caller 0x1343ab4c4dcf8191d of the token for 1e12 wei of currency0, the second takes in 0x1a4aecd652ac4ec5441d of the token, equal to the whole PoolManager balance, for 0xc83cab48385e (about 0.00022) of currency0. The pool books an inflow of 124,163e18 tokens while the PoolManager balance does not rise, which is the token's own accounting at work, a hazard of that token's LPs only. No currency other than the token and WETH moves, and the WETH amounts are dust. I agree with the class; the row needs no network property. I did not run the other 9,400 rows.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1: the cycle 6 outflow rule as census2.py applies it, with its blind spots (a) to (h): native outflows on 20 of 21 networks, currencies of pools with a ModifyLiquidity log in the transaction, unknown pools, wrong amounts the PoolManager computes and logs, ERC-6909 transfers between accounts, unlogged balance changes, freezes, and inflows larger than owed.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I read census2.py lines 60 to 140. Transfer logs count only with three topics and 32 bytes of data, Deposit logs count as inflow, Swap amounts are read as signed int128, ERC-6909 Transfer logs with four topics count as mints when topic1 is zero and burns when topic2 is zero, and a row is skipped as native-no-logs when the currency is address 0 and no native log exists. In src/ the Swap event at src/PoolManager.sol:241-250 is emitted from the same delta that _swap returns (src/PoolManager.sol:234-252), before any afterSwap hook delta, so an arithmetic fault in Pool.swap would be booked as owed, as the item says. ModifyLiquidity carries only liquidityDelta and salt (src/PoolManager.sol:175). collectProtocolFees emits nothing (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57) and is gated to the fee controller at line 48, with the synced currency check at lines 49-52. ERC-6909 transfer and transferFrom log with both addresses nonzero (src/ERC6909.sol:30, 45). The listed blind spots are real and the item states them; the clearance is therefore narrow and says nothing about native currency, liquidity removals or arithmetic. The high priority lead to widen the census to those three gaps is the right next step.
